stumbles.quote: Jev is not joining the public posting review.
stumbles.why: Jev is introduced without saying who or what it is beyond a vague description, and the 'public posting review' process is never explained. Oskar is also not introduced.

stumbles.quote: Jev had done well on routing questions.
stumbles.why: This refers to earlier work that the text doesn't describe. The reader can't tell what routing questions were or how Jev did on them.
The tool is named but never explained. The reader doesn't know what it flags or what a 'hit' is.
'Tic' is never defined in the text. It only points to a definition in register.md, which the reader can't see.
The file and the definition are not explained or included, so the reader doesn't know what the tic is.

stumbles.quote: A baseline that knows only the hit's lint category, which gives it the category's historical tic rate
stumbles.why: The source of the 'historical' rate is unclear. If it came from these same 261 labelled hits, the comparison is leaky. The text doesn't say.

stumbles.quote: At a 5% error budget it could settle only 24.5% of hits on its own
stumbles.why: 'Settle' and 'error budget' are not defined. The reader can't tell what settling a hit means or how the 5% is measured. The headline says 'a quarter', which loosely matches 24.5%.

stumbles.quote: the bar set in advance was 50%
stumbles.why: The reader doesn't know who set the bar or why it was 50%. It is also unclear whether the 50% refers to the share of hits settled.

stumbles.quote: At a 0.5 threshold that baseline beat Jev on accuracy, 0.751 to 0.732.
stumbles.why: It is unclear which Jev variant this compares against, with or without the definition. The baseline also beats Jev on accuracy but loses on AUROC, and the text doesn't reconcile the two.

stumbles.quote: 5 of 44 triad hits were real tics, as were 5 of 43 participle hits and 16 of 18 negation-first hits.
stumbles.why: 'Triad', 'participle' and 'negation-first' are lint rules that are never explained. The counts are also not tied to the 261 agreed hits, and they don't visibly add up to the 35.2% rate.

point: Jev, a small calibrated decision model, was tested on labelled lint hits. It beat a category-only baseline on ranking but not on accuracy, and it settled only about a quarter of hits against a 50% target, so it isn't going into public posting review.
